title: Capability status record
description: One row of the observed-readiness layer: what was last actually verified, when, and with what caveat. Routes say what is possible; status rows say what was last proven; only a fresh probe says it works right now. The required fields are the compact record. The optional fields below are documented extensions an adopter may add; an added field that carries authority must be validated by the same contract tests that cover the compact record, or it becomes decoration that readers trust and nothing enforces.

state.description: The degradation taxonomy. source-ready-live-inactive means fully built, registered, probed and tested while deliberately not wired into any live client; activation is a separate approval.

support_class.description: Finer-grained than state, for example supported, built-in, legacy, experimental, supported-read-only, or supported-secret-safe-readiness.

freshness_class.description: Encodes reprobe policy on the row itself, deciding whether the registry row, the status row, or a fresh probe is sufficient for a given action class.

provenance.description: Optional documented extension, not part of the compact record. How strongly the capability is backed: written rule only, a checked-in helper enforcing it, runtime code implementing it, or evidence that it has been exercised in production. Carrying it on the row is a design choice; the taxonomy itself is a property of the capability either way.

route_ref.description: Optional documented extension, not part of the compact record. The integration route this row was proven against, if any.

probe_ref.description: Optional documented extension, not part of the compact record. The probe whose run produced the evidence.

evidence.description: Pointer to the artifact or probe run that substantiates the state. A row with no evidence pointer is an assertion, not a status.

constraint_or_fallback.description: The constraint in force, or the sanctioned fallback lane. Rendered into the generated operator view.
